candidate.title: addGuests loads booking by raw id (with heavy includes) before authorization, enabling cross-tenant probing/enumeration
reports: booking lookup findfirst({ where: { id } }) is not scoped to the requester's team/user before loading organizer details and credentials (addguests.handler.ts:43-49)

heavy multi-include fetch (attendees, references, eventtype, owner + credentials) in addguests.handler.ts executes before the authorization check for any bookingid from any authenticated user, enabling cheap-for-attacker full-materialization probing; notfound throws before forbidden so booking existence is also enumerable

[bug] the booking lookup by { id: bookingid } has no scoping to the requesting user's owned/organized bookings or team membership at the query level, and eventtype teamid is used for authorization even when booking.eventtype is null (eventtype is optional in the include and the code writes booking.eventtype?.teamid ?? 0). for personal bookings (no eventtype), isteamadmin/isteamowner are called with teamid 0 and return false, so authorization silently depends only on organizer/attendee match; a null eventtype on a team-booked booking also bypasses the team path. any knowledge of a numeric bookingid plus attendee identity is the only gate on mutating someone else's booking.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addguests.handler.ts:26-56 — p2, confidence medium: prisma.booking.findfirst({ where: { id: bookingid } }) fetches the booking unscoped to the requesting user before any authorization check, so any authenticated user (any bookingid, including other tenants' bookings) can trigger the query and reach the permission-check branch; combined with the isteamadminorowner bug below, current effective authorization collapses to organizer-or-attendee, but the unscoped lookup pattern is fragile — a future edit to the && (see next finding) or any bypass of isorganizer/isattendee reintroduces full idor to add guests/send calendar invites on arbitrary bookings.
